psychApp.practiceMetaDescription: Meditation benefits, audio sessions and videos.
psychApp.whatText: Meditation is the practice of gathering the mind into the present moment. There is no opponent and no win: only breath, body and attention. Research shows a regular practice lowers stress hormones, lengthens attention span and improves sleep quality. Five minutes a day is enough to begin.
psychApp.benefit1Desc: Instead of a storm of thoughts — observing: thoughts come back, you watch.
psychApp.benefit2Desc: The 4-7-8 rhythm activates the parasympathetic system — the body settles.
psychApp.benefit3Desc: An evening practice shortens the way to sleep and deepens the night.
psychApp.benefit4Desc: The gap between stimulus and response widens — choice returns.
psychApp.benefit5Desc: Regular practice strengthens the focus muscle — at work and in relationships.
psychApp.benefit6Desc: The body scan teaches where feelings live in the body — powerful alongside the journal.

psychApp.psyAidaEdu: MA in psychology, Baku State University (2010). Started clinical work in hospital centers in Baku; running a private practice for individual and trauma-focused sessions since 2012. Has led the EMDR supervision group for the past five years.
psychApp.psyLeylaEdu: BA in psychology, Azerbaijan State Pedagogical University (2013). Specialized in small groups: running online group sessions since 2015, and delivering corporate workshops as a mindfulness instructor.
psychApp.psySamirEdu: BSU, psychology (2014). Known for evening-cabinet individual sessions; partners with consulting firms on work stress and team dynamics. Works with an ACT + CBT blend.
psychApp.psyGulshanEdu: MA in clinical psychology, Ankara University, Türkiye (2008). Combines the Gottman method with a systemic approach in couples and family sessions. Seeing clients in her own office since 2010.
psychApp.psyKamranEdu: BSU, psychology (2012), child & adolescent specialization (2014). Six years as a school psychologist; opened his own practice in play therapy and parent consultations.
psychApp.psyNarimanEdu: Clinical psychology, Khazar University, Baku (2009). Completed international certification programs in trauma; running trauma sessions online since 2011 and supervising in non-profit projects.
psychApp.psyElmiraEdu: BSU master's (2011), doctoral coursework in family therapy. Working with family systems since 2013; sees clients both in-office and online.
psychApp.psyRasimEdu: ASPU (2015). Focused on young professionals and students; trained in ACT, running online group and individual sessions since 2017.
psychApp.psyAidaRules: Sessions run 50 minutes. Cancellation is free up to 24 hours in advance; later notice bills half the session. In urgent situations the psychologist reaches out herself.
psychApp.psyLeylaRules: Group sessions start on time — entry closes after a 5-minute grace window. What is said in the group stays in the group: confidentiality first.
psychApp.psySamirRules: Evening hours are in demand — bookings are confirmed 48 hours ahead. Session notes are prepared on request.
psychApp.psyGulshanRules: In couples work both partners must attend the first session. Payment before the session; cancellation up to 48 hours.
psychApp.psyKamranRules: Child sessions run 45 minutes; the parent joins the first and last 10 minutes. Nothing is done without the child's consent.
psychApp.psyNarimanRules: Trauma work proceeds step by step — no step is compulsory. Online sessions require a calm, stable connection.
psychApp.psyElmiraRules: In family sessions every member's voice weighs equally. The first session is an introduction — no decisions are made on day one.
psychApp.psyRasimRules: The first consultation is free for young clients. Small between-session exercises are offered — always optional.

gymApp.exRunGuide: Start at an easy pace and nudge the speed up after two minutes. Stay at a conversational effort — the goal of a warm-up is to wake up, not to tire.
gymApp.exStretchGuide: Hold each muscle group in a gentle stretch for 20-30 seconds; no bouncing. Keep breathing steadily — the tension softens with the breath.
gymApp.exSquatGuide: Bar on the shoulders, feet shoulder-width. Knees track over the toes as you sink, chest proud, back tight. Descend until the hips pass the knees, then drive up.
gymApp.exDeadliftGuide: Bar over mid-foot, back flat, chest ahead of hips. Bend the knees, then stand up keeping the bar close to the body. Finish tall — no leaning back.
gymApp.exBenchGuide: Lie on the bench, shoulder blades pinched, feet planted. Lower the bar to mid-chest, pause a beat, then press up hard. Wrists stay straight.
gymApp.exPullupGuide: Grip just wider than the shoulders. Pull the shoulder blades down and slightly back, then drive the body up until the chin clears the bar. Lower with control; if full reps are too hard, start with a band or negatives.
gymApp.exRowGuide: Hinge to 45 degrees with the bar hanging. Row it toward the lower ribs, squeeze for a beat, lower slowly. The back stays flat throughout.
gymApp.exOhpGuide: Standing, bar at the shoulders. Brace the core and press straight overhead — the bar passes the face on the same line, finishing over the ears with locked arms.
gymApp.exLungeGuide: Step one foot forward and lower until the back knee hovers near the floor. The front knee stays behind the toes, torso upright. Drive back up and switch legs.
gymApp.exPlankGuide: Elbows under the shoulders, body one straight line. Hips neither pike up nor sag — keep breathing and draw the navel in.
gymApp.exSwingGuide: Hold the kettlebell with both hands and drive with the hips — the arms stay relaxed. Power comes from the hips; the bell floats to chest height. The back never rounds.
gymApp.exLegpressGuide: Feet shoulder-width on the platform, knees tracking the toes. Lower to about 90 degrees and press up without locking out. The lower back stays glued to the seat.
gymApp.exLatpullGuide: Take a wide grip and lean back slightly. Pull the bar to the upper chest, squeeze the lats, release slowly. Think of pulling with the back, not the hands.
gymApp.exBicepGuide: Elbows close to the body, curl the dumbbells up one smooth arc. No wrist swing — the movement lives in the elbow. Lower slowly.
gymApp.exTricepsGuide: At the cable station, elbows pinned to the sides; press down until the arms fully extend. Return slowly — the elbows never drift forward.

blurb.deepwork: Newport shows the real cost of fragmented attention and gives concrete rules that protect deep concentration. Every chapter ends with a tool you can turn into a habit.
blurb.habits: Clear breaks a habit into four laws — cue, craving, response, reward — and turns each into small steps you can apply today.
blurb.meaning: Drawing on the camp experience, Frankl shows that finding meaning is a choice. One of the rare books that changes what a life means.
blurb.thinking: Kahneman separates the mind's two systems — fast intuition and slow logic — and pinpoints exactly where we go wrong.
blurb.meditations: The Roman emperor's notes to himself — the most personal source of Stoic practice. Short, heavy, openable any day.
blurb.flow: Csikszentmihalyi studies full absorption — flow: when, how and why some hours simply fly.
